title: ACVA-Bench: Beyond Prompt Following in Abstract Concept Visualization Ability for Text-to-Image Models
title_zh: ACVA-Bench：超越提示词跟随的文生图模型抽象概念可视化能力评测

paragraphs.en: 提出ACVA-Bench基准，从语义充分性、多样性与区分性三维度评测文生图模型的抽象概念可视化能力。 Text-to-image (T2I) models have achieved remarkable progress in image quality and instruction following, prompting growing research interest in their capacity for deep understanding that goes beyond literal prompt matching. However, without an explicit visual scheme provided, it remains unclear and has not been systematically evaluated whether T2I models can autonomously translate abstract concepts lacking a fixed visual referent, such as "loyalty," into visual representations that are accurate, diverse, and distinguishable from closely related concepts. We define this capability as Abstract Concept Visualization Ability (ACVA) and introduce ACVA-Bench, a category-balanced benchmark grounded in psycholinguistic norms of abstract concepts, which examines models' ACVA along three dimensions semantic sufficiency, representational diversity, and conceptual distinctiveness under a low-intervention setting that withholds concrete objects, scenes, or visual metaphors. Since abstract concepts lack a unique reference image, conventional evaluation metrics that rely on reference-image matching are difficult to apply. To address this, we propose a fine-grained visual-semantic evaluation method constrained by concept semantics, which decomposes concept semantics into independently verifiable visual-semantic questions to assess the semantic representation quality of generated images, with its validity further confirmed by human evaluation. Benchmarking results on mainstream T2I models show that these models rely on a small set of prototypical visual patterns, leaving room for improvement in representational diversity and conceptual distinctiveness for abstract concepts, thereby providing an interpretable and reproducible evaluation foundation for future research.
paragraphs.zh: 提出ACVA-Bench基准，从语义充分性、多样性与区分性三维度评测文生图模型的抽象概念可视化能力。文生图（T2I）模型在图像质量和指令遵循方面取得了显著进展，这引发了人们对其深层理解能力的日益增长的研究兴趣，即超越字面提示匹配的能力。 然而，在没有提供明确视觉方案的情况下，文生图模型能否自主地将缺乏固定视觉指涉对象的抽象概念（如“忠诚”）转化为准确、多样且与相近概念可区分的视觉表现，这一问题仍不清楚，也未曾得到系统性评估。 我们将这种能力定义为抽象概念可视化能力（ACVA），并引入ACVA-Bench，这是一个基于心理语言学抽象概念规范、类别均衡的基准，在低干预设置下（即不提供具体物体、场景或视觉隐喻），从语义充分性、表现多样性和概念区分性三个维度考察模型的抽象概念可视化能力。 由于抽象概念缺乏唯一的参考图像，依赖参考图像匹配的传统评估指标难以应用。 为解决这一问题，我们提出一种受概念语义约束的细粒度视觉-语义评估方法，该方法将概念语义分解为可独立验证的视觉-语义问题，以评估生成图像的语义表现质量，其有效性进一步通过人工评估得到确认。 对主流文生图模型的基准测试结果显示，这些模型依赖于一小组原型化的视觉模式，在抽象概念的表现多样性和概念区分性方面仍有改进空间，从而为未来研究提供了一个可解释、可复现的评估基础。
